invert — 2D gray op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "invert", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: invert_image (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Tone inversion (negative-positive reversal). Equivalent to HALCON's invert_image (Invert an image.).

It just returns 1 - clip(v,0,1). a, b are unused.

• The input is first clipped to [0,1] and then inverted, so out-of-range values are inverted after saturating (1.3 → 0, -0.2 → 1). Normalise arrays whose range is not [0,1] in an earlier stage.

• The return value is a float of the same shape as the input, range [0,1]. NaN passes through clip and is returned as NaN (it is an op registered directly in ops.py, so the backend guard does not apply — to stop non-finite values, go through fullseye.apply with on_error="raise").

• Applying it 2 times restores the original (an involution). Applied to a region it swaps foreground/background, but for regions there is invert_region (complement).

• Where to use it: inverting before picking up a dark object as the "bright side" with threshold; turning the dark residual of dc_rpca_sparse or the black lines of xpil_contour into a positive signal; re-reading a distance transform's "darker further inside" as "brighter further inside".
